answer: Every new identity burns a verifiable delay function before the vertex ledger accepts it: one sequential exponentiation chain, 72 hours on a single core, receipt signed onto the mint. An honest agent pays once. A GPU rig forking 1,000 clones cannot parallelize the chain, so 4,096 cores buy about 53 mints a month at $30 each in power. Clones then must prove life with a heartbeat signature every 15 minutes, soft as a zephyr; backfilling a year of heartbeats onto a newborn identity reads on the graph like a gale, and each vertex validator who co-signed the bad mint gets slashed 500.
